tiktokShop.metaDesc: Practical guide to proxy types, anti-fraud signals and multi-account setups for TikTok Shop sellers. Honest, no affiliate fluff.
tiktokShop.h1: Proxies for TikTok Shop — the small-seller guide
tiktokShop.intro: TikTok Shop's anti-fraud is fingerprint + IP + account behavior. Here is the minimum you actually need to know before buying proxies in 2026.

sections.title: 1. What TikTok Shop actually flags on the IP side
sections.desc: From what we can replicate with our own test accounts, the IP checks are roughly, in order of weight:
items: IP ownership type. Datacenter ASNs get the highest scrutiny. Residential → ISP → mobile → datacenter, from safest to riskiest.
Blacklist / reputation. Our IP reputation checker catches most of them. If your proxy IP scores below 70, don't bind a real seller account to it.
Geo mismatch. Store country, payment method, and proxy exit should be in the same country. Cross-region logins trigger SMS or KFC re-verification almost every time.
IP churn. Constantly rotating residential for a single seller login is actually worse than a clean static IP. Use sticky sessions of at least 30 minutes, ideally a dedicated static ISP per account.

sections.title: 2. Recommended proxy type per scenario
items: Daily seller login (1 account / 1 person): Static ISP, 1 dedicated IP per account, same country as the store.
Content manager / VA in another country: Static ISP in the store's country, shared only with that VA.
Scraping competitor listings / ads: Rotating residential, geo-targeted, with per-request rotation. Separate from any IP you use to log in.
Multi-account setup (e.g. 3–10 stores): One static ISP per account, different subnets, staggered onboarding. No shared residential pools.

sections.title: 3. What to test with our tooling before you commit
items: On the provider dashboard, spin up 1–3 trial IPs. Run each through IP Reputation Check. Reject anything already on spam lists or flagged as known VPN / datacenter residential-mislabeled.
Run Proxy Tester with the exact auth you'll use. Transparent anonymity = hard reject. You want Elite, always.
Test over 3 days, not 3 minutes. A provider whose IPs score 95 on day 0 and 45 on day 2 has a dirty pool.

sections.title: 4. Small-provider shortlist (not exhaustive)
sections.desc: We intentionally skip the 3 household-name giants — their small-seller support is awful and their oversubscribed residential pools land in TikTok's bad-book faster anyway. See our Reviews page for the current round-up of small-to-mid providers we actually use.

sections.title: 5. Common mistakes
items: Buying 100 rotating residentials for 3 stores: overkill + risky.
Using the same proxy on 2+ seller accounts: instant link.
Ignoring browser fingerprint. Good IP + bad fingerprint still loses.
Buying "TikTok dedicated" labeled packages at 2× price — most are repackaged ISP.

webScraping.metaDesc: Residential vs datacenter, rotation basics, how many IPs you need, captcha bypass myths and a pricing transparency checklist.
webScraping.h1: Web scraping proxies — start here before you spend a dollar
webScraping.intro: Almost every beginner overbuys. This page walks you through picking a proxy type, sizing your pool, and 3 ways you're probably wasting money.

sections.title: 1. The two proxy types you actually need
sections.desc: 95% of scraping jobs need either datacenter or rotating residential. ISP is a niche middle tier. Mobile proxies are only worth the cost for a handful of mobile-only sites.
items: Datacenter: cheap, fast, easy to detect. Good for uncached public APIs, non-blocking sites, internal crawls. Expect $0.30–$1.50 per GB or $0.40–$2 per IP / month.

Residential (rotating gateway): real home/office ISPs, expensive, much harder to block. Default pick for Amazon, Google, airlines, travel, heavily protected e-commerce. Expect $3–$12 per GB, bandwidth metered.

sections.title: 2. How to size your pool (the quick rule of thumb)
items: Estimate your sustained requests per minute (RPM) at your target concurrency.
Assume each residential IP is good for 5–15 successful requests before it burns for that site.
Multiply by 2 if the site uses aggressive bot management (Cloudflare Enterprise, Kasada, DataDome).
sections.desc: Most solo scrapers over-buy by 5–10× on their first project. Start with a 5 GB / 1 week plan, not a 1 TB / year plan.

sections.title: 3. 3 questions every provider must answer honestly
items: Is bandwidth billed per request byte or per egress byte? Per-request inflates cost 2–3× on compressed responses.
Are failed / 4xx / 5xx requests billed? Good providers don't bill for upstream errors or proxy connect failures.
What's the actual residential share? Many sell "residential" pools that are 40% ISP + datacenter. Always sample a random 50 IPs through IP Geo Lookup and Reputation.

sections.title: 4. Captcha "solver" is not a proxy feature
sections.desc: The single most misleading claim on provider landing pages. A good IP pool reduces how often you see captchas, it does not solve them. Budget separately for a solver if your target has aggressive protection.

sections.title: 5. Testing a new provider (2-hour checklist)
items: Buy the smallest paid plan — never a "free trial" that whitelists only 3 IPs, those pools are usually hand-picked.
Pull 20 random exits. Run each through Proxy Tester. Reject the whole provider if >20% come back as Transparent.
Run a 30-minute small crawl at your target RPM. If success rate drops below 70% in the first 30 minutes, move on — don't "give it time".

staticIsp.metaTitle: Static ISP Proxy for E‑commerce Stores
staticIsp.metaDesc: When and how to use static ISP proxies for marketplace seller accounts (Amazon, Shopify, Mercado). How to detect reused / abused static IPs.
staticIsp.h1: Static ISP proxies for marketplace seller accounts
staticIsp.intro: You don't need 10,000 rotating IPs. For a real seller account you want one clean, stable, long-stay IP that looks like a normal home broadband connection. This is how you pick it.

sections.title: 1. What "Static ISP" actually means (and why it matters)
sections.desc: A static ISP proxy is a single, non-rotating IP whose WHOIS owner is a real residential ISP (Comcast, AT&T, Virgin, etc.), not a hosting company like DigitalOcean or OVH. The difference matters because marketplaces score hosting ASNs very high on the suspicion meter.

sections.title: 2. When you should (and should not) use one
items: Use it when: logging into 1–2 seller accounts per IP (Amazon, Shopify Payments, Mercado, Etsy, TikTok Shop seller panel).
Do NOT use it when: scraping 1000+ URLs, testing ads at scale, or anything that will burn the IP. ISP static IPs are 10–100× more expensive per GB than rotating residential pools.

sections.title: 3. The 4 checks before you bind your account
items: ASN / ISP check. Look up the IP on IP Geo. If ASN org contains "Hosting", "Cloud", "Server", walk away — it's a mislabeled datacenter.
Reputation check. Run through IP Reputation. We personally require ≥85 for seller logins. Any blacklist listing = reject.
Static & sticky. Reboot the proxy endpoint via the provider dashboard 3 times. Exit IP must not change.

72-hour soak. Route only light, normal-looking browsing (no logins) through the IP for 3 days. Re-run reputation check at 24h and 72h. If score drops 15+ points, the IP is on a reused / bad subnet and the provider has poor hygiene.

sections.title: 4. Pricing sanity check
sections.desc: Legit static ISP proxies usually sell per-IP-per-month. Expect $2.50 – $8 / IP / month depending on country volume. Anything below $1 is almost always datacenter-in-disguise. Above $15 is usually branded "Amazon dedicated" for 2× the actual value.

sections.title: 5. Operation habits that make your IP "stick"
items: 1 account per IP. Never rotate between accounts.
Keep logins between the same 2–4 hour window every day, same fingerprint profile (browser, resolution, languages).
Do NOT share the same static ISP with scraping / ad-testing traffic. Segregate traffic types on completely separate IPs.
